bull.b: Very low leverage and substantial equity resources give CG Oncology financial flexibility to continue clinical development without relying heavily on debt. This strengthens resilience through upcoming trial milestones and provides capacity to fund operations while preserving strategic options.

Progress in a Phase 3 program and publication of additional clinical results strengthen the evidence base for cretostimogene. These milestones can support regulatory preparation, potential commercialization efforts, and longer-term differentiation in high-risk non-muscle invasive bladder cancer.

Revenue growth indicates some improvement in commercial or collaboration-related traction despite the company remaining clinical-stage. If sustained, a growing revenue base could gradually offset development spending and provide a broader foundation for future operating leverage.

bear.b: The scale of operating losses remains disproportionate to revenue, showing that the current business model has not yet converted development activity into sustainable profitability. Continued losses could require prolonged external funding and increase the risk of shareholder dilution.

Heavy negative operating and free cash flow means CG Oncology consumes substantial cash to advance its programs rather than internally funding growth. Even with a strong cash position, sustained burn reduces financial durability and makes future capital needs dependent on execution and funding access.

Expenses are expanding faster than the revenue base, indicating limited operating leverage at the current development stage. Unless clinical progress eventually supports meaningful revenue growth, rising R&D and administrative costs can keep margins under pressure and prolong the path to profitability.
